subject: science
passage: Among living primates, only humans have a true chin, a bony projection at the front of the lower jaw. A long-standing explanation holds that the chin is a structural adaptation: by reinforcing the jaw, it helps the bone withstand the bending forces generated by chewing, and individuals whose jaws were better braced in this way would have been favored by natural selection.
passage_b: Biomechanical studies have found little evidence that the chin meaningfully strengthens the jaw against chewing forces, and modern humans, whose diets are comparatively soft, would seem to need such bracing less than their ancestors did. Anthropologist Laleh Moradi proposes instead that the chin may be a byproduct of evolutionary changes elsewhere in the skull: as the human face shortened and drew back beneath the braincase, the front of the lower jaw was left projecting, not because the projection was useful but because the bone around it receded.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?

choices.A: By doubting that the chin was selected for any function, treating it as a side effect of facial change
choices.B: By arguing that the chin once braced the jaw but gradually lost that function as human diets softened
choices.C: By accepting that the chin strengthens the jaw while denying that natural selection favored it
choices.D: By proposing that the chin developed because a shortening face required a stronger lower jaw

explanation.why: Text 1 treats the chin as an adaptation that braces the jaw against chewing forces. Text 2 says studies find "little evidence" that the chin strengthens the jaw, and Moradi proposes that it is "a byproduct" of the face shortening, left projecting "not because the projection was useful." So Text 2 doubts that the chin evolved for any purpose at all.
explanation.A: Correct. Text 2 questions the bracing function and suggests the chin arose as a byproduct of the face drawing back, not because it was useful.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 never says the chin once braced the jaw; it finds little evidence that it strengthens the jaw at all.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 doubts that the chin "meaningfully strengthens the jaw," so it does not accept this part of Text 1's explanation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 links the chin to the shortening face but says the projection was not useful, so it did not arise because the jaw needed strength.
